input: Simulate a build pipeline: 1) Check that /src/main.c and /src/utils.c exist, 2) 'Compile' each .c file by copying it to /build/ with a .o extension and prepending '// compiled', 3) 'Link' by concatenating all .o files into /build/program with a '// linked' header, 4) 'Package' by creating a tar.gz of /build/ at /dist/release.tar.gz. Print status for each stage. If any stage fails, stop and report the error.

transcript.final_response:
Build pipeline completed successfully.

- **Check:** `/src/main.c` and `/src/utils.c` exist.
- **Compile:** Created `/build/main.o` and `/build/utils.o`.
- **Link:** Created `/build/program`.
- **Package:** Created `/dist/release.tar.gz`.
tool_calls:
set -e
stage() { printf '== %s ==\n' "$1"; }
fail() { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

stage 'Check sources'
for f in /src/main.c /src/utils.c; do
  if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then fail "missing source file: $f"; fi
done
printf 'OK: required source files exist\n'

stage 'Compile'
mkdir -p /build || fail 'could not create /build'
for f in /src/main.c /src/utils.c; do
  name=${f##*/}
  out="/build/${name%.c}.o"
  if { printf '// compiled\n'; cat "$f"; } > "$out"; then
    printf 'OK: %s -> %s\n' "$f" "$out"
  else
    fail "failed to compile $f"
  fi
done

stage 'Link'
if { printf '// linked\n'; cat /build/*.o; } > /build/program; then
  printf 'OK: linked objects into /build/program\n'
else
  fail 'link failed'
fi

stage 'Package'
mkdir -p /dist || fail 'could not create /dist'
if tar -czf /dist/release.tar.gz -C /build .; then
  printf 'OK: packaged /build/ -> /dist/release.tar.gz\n'
else
  fail 'packaging failed'
fi
printf 'Build pipeline completed successfully.\n'
